title: Orbiting Request Synthesis: Sales/CS Enterprise Asks Consolidation & Quick-Scoping Hub
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Problem: Sales and CS submit many similar but slightly divergent enterprise feature requests that 'orbit'—they reappear in different accounts and regions, with subtle differences (eg. VPC + custom KMS, data residency, throughput SLAs). This causes duplicate scoping effort, inconsistent proposals to customers, and slow sales cycles.

Goal: Build a lightweight synthesis & quick-scoping hub (internal tool + checklist + templated mini-PRD) that turns a batch of related Sales/CS enterprise asks into: 1) a canonical request cluster, 2) an initial implementation pathway (self-serve / dedicated / private + estimated econ), and 3) a one-page summary for Sales/CS and Solutions Engineering within 48 hours.

Success metrics: 
- Reduce duplicate scoping work by 60% for repeated asks within 90 days.
- Median time-to-first-scope (internal one-pager) <= 48 hours.
- Increase conversion from ask -> opportunity-qualified brief to Eng by 30% for enterprise pipeline.

Out of scope: Full engineering design or delivery. This is an intake/synthesis and initial scoping layer only.
proposal:
1) Intake Aggregator: lightweight form used by Sales/CS (prefilled from SFDC snippets) that tags requests with account, compliance flags, throughput expectations, and preferred deployment mode.
2) Automated clustering: weekly job that groups similar asks (by tags + short text embeddings) into 'orbit clusters' for review.
3) Quick-Scoping Template: a 1-page mini-PRD with: problem statement, proposed route (hosted/dedicated/private), key constraints, rough effort bucket (S/M/L), ballpark cost delta, compliance blockers, and suggested next step (pilot, engage SE, or roadmap).
4) Triage Roster: rotation of PM + Solutions Eng + Sales rep to review clusters and publish canonical brief.
5) Ops artifacts: GitHub issue template + tracking label + onboarding note for Eng when escalated.

Trade-offs considered: automated clustering reduces manual triage but will miss nuanced compliance differences; the hub should prioritize human review for clusters with 'compliance' or 'SLA' tags. We will aim for high-precision clustering for low-risk asks and force manual path for high-risk ones.
acceptance_criteria:
- Intake form prototype available and connected to sample SFDC exports.
- Weekly clustering job produces clusters for a 30-account sample and presents them to the triage roster.
- One-page quick-scope template created and used to produce 10 canonical briefs.
- Stakeholder signoffs: Sales leader, Head of Solutions Eng, Security PM.
- Dashboard: time-to-scope metric visible in Console/PM dashboard.
outcomes_and_metrics:
- 60% reduction in repeat scoping work for similar asks (90-day lookback).
- Median time-to-first-scope <= 48 hours for clustered asks.
- 30% higher ask->brief qualification rate.
- Track number of clusters escalated to Eng and time-to-onboard into Eng backlog.
risks:
- Embedding-based clustering may conflate feature semantics across deployment modes (eg. 'custom audit logs' in hosted vs private). Mitigation: require explicit deployment-mode tag during submission.
- Resource overhead for weekly triage; mitigation: 2-week rotation and initially limit to accounts > $50k ARR.
- Inaccurate econ estimates could mislead Sales; mitigation: provide ranges and link to Cost Estimator tool rather than single-point numbers.
implementation_notes:
Engineering will expose a small endpoint to accept CSV/SFDC snippets. Initial clustering will run in a sandbox notebook from Research (use embeddings from Optimize's evaluators). Quick-scope template stored in Confluence and converted to a GitHub issue when escalated. Keep templates minimal and iterate after 10 customer briefs.

Estimated eng effort to support: small (<2 wks) for integration + 1 sprint for triage tooling. Will use existing labeling and routing in Console; no infra changes expected for MVP.
